# satisfied by

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:satisfiedBy`](gmeow-satisfiedBy.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/satisfiedBy>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/teleology`](../../slices/teleology.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

Relates a goal to a situation that counts as achieving it. NOT functional: many situations may satisfy one goal, and disputed satisfaction is several coexisting vantage-indexed claims through the statement layer — never a global verdict ([Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)).

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:Goal`](../classes/gmeow-Goal.md) -> [`gufo:Situation`](http://purl.org/nemo/gufo#Situation)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:satisfiedBy`](gmeow-satisfiedBy.md) from [`gmeow:Goal`](../classes/gmeow-Goal.md) to [`gufo:Situation`](http://purl.org/nemo/gufo#Situation) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to record that a particular situation counts as achieving a goal — the achievement link a renderer or planner reads to ask whether a goal has been met.

### Avoid when

- Avoid asserting a single canonical satisfaction when achievement is contested; carry each contested judgement on the statement with [`gmeow:accordingTo`](gmeow-accordingTo.md) ([Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)), and never make this functional — many situations may satisfy one goal.

### How to use

- Point the [`Goal`](../classes/gmeow-Goal.md) at one or more [gufo:Situation](http://purl.org/nemo/gufo#Situation) individuals; for disputed achievement, mint coexisting gmeow:accordingTo-annotated statements rather than forcing the reasoner to pick a winner, and leave means-end search to the solver layer ([Principle 12](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-12)).
